facts.fact: ModernGhana says Niger's media regulator ONC suspended nine French-language outlets (including AFP, TV5 Monde, Jeune Afrique, Mediapart and TF1 Info) in a single order in May 2026, citing threats to public order, national unity and the stability of republican institutions.
facts.system: ONC suspension of nine French-language media outlets

facts.fact: ModernGhana says investigative editor Ali Soumana of Le Courrier was jailed in September 2025 after a complaint from the Prime Minister over a customs-fraud report (defamation complaint).
ModernGhana says the BBC was suspended in Niger in December 2024; the document gives no reason for the suspension.

ModernGhana says Soumana Maiga of L'Enquêteur was arrested in April 2024 and charged with harming national defence after his paper reported on Russian listening equipment allegedly installed on state buildings.

ModernGhana says the Ministry of the Interior forced the Maison de la Presse, the umbrella body of journalists' associations, to shut down in January 2024 after it spoke out against post-coup press violations.
ModernGhana says Samira Sabou was detained incommunicado for eight days in September 2023 over reporting deemed likely to disturb public order.
ModernGhana says the signals of RFI and France 24 were cut within a week of the July 2023 coup; the document gives no reason.

facts.fact: Human Rights Watch states that on 30 October 2025 Niamey police arrested six journalists (Moussa Kaka and Abdoul Aziz of Radio Television Saraounia, Ibro Chaibou and Souleymane Brah of Voix du Peuple, Youssouf Seriba of Les Echos du Niger, Oumarou Kane of Le Herisson), three of them held at Kollo prison, and charged all six with complicity in circulating a document likely to disturb public order under the 2019 cybercrime law, apparently over sharing on social media an invitation to a state press conference announcing new mandatory levies for the security-forces solidarity fund.
facts.system: Six Nigerien journalists arrested under the 2019 cybercrime law

facts.fact: Human Rights Watch says lawyer Abrourahamane Lirwana was charged and detained from 21 September 2026 over comments about the army, apparently a 12 September Facebook post, and prosecutors sought five years on 6 October.

note: Journalist Moussa Kaka's detention is not recorded: the document says authorities have not named his offence.

facts.fact: Niger's National Communication Observatory (ONC) said on 8 May 2026 it was suspending nine France-based outlets (France 24, RFI, AFP, TV5Monde, Jeune Afrique, Mediapart, TF1 Info, LSI Africa, France Afrique Media) over content it said threatened public order, as reported by CPJ.
CPJ reports the ONC suspended nine outlets from reaching audiences in Niger, with a France 24 channel screen showing 'program blocked'.

note: Ordinance restores prison terms for online defamation and prosecutors are instructed, but no one is reported charged; a speech law places nothing.
Document states nothing the study asks for this country.

facts.fact: MFWA says journalist Ibro Chaibou was freed on 28 August 2026 after nearly ten months in detention, charged over sharing an invitation to a press conference.
MFWA says authorities suspended nine international media outlets in Niger in May 2026, including France 24, RFI and AFP.
CPJ reports DW Hausa correspondent Gazali Abdou Tasawa was jailed in Niamey on 23 January 2026 after police questioning over his 15 January report on Nigerian refugees.
CPJ reports that five journalists were behind bars in Niger on 1 December 2025 in its annual prison census, over reporting questioning governance.

note: Document announces prison terms for online defamation, a law placing nothing until someone is charged; no charge is reported.

facts.fact: ANLC/TI-Niger, reporting its Niamey workshop with ministries, civil society and media, said the 2011 access to information ordinance still has no implementing decree and that the 2024 cybercrime ordinance raises concern for its repressive use against journalists and activists.
